user_questions.question: Your requirement contradicts itself: gift certificates 'must never expire' and 'all gift certificates should auto-expire after 12 months'. Which rule should the design implement? (A) Expire after 12 months except when the recipient Contact's mailing state is California (no state field exists on Gift_Certificate__c; would derive from Recipient__c -> Contact); (B) By Gift_Certificate__c.Type__c: Purchased never expires; promotional types (Recovery, Promotion, Loyalty Reward, Referral Bonus) expire 12 months after Issue_Date__c; (C) No certificate expires; (D) All expire after 12 months. Evidence: Type__c picklist is Purchased/Recovery/Promotion/Loyalty Reward/Referral Bonus; IssueGiftCardAction currently hardcodes a 90-day expiry; nothing marks certificates Expired. Recommendation: B, since California law bars expiry on sold certificates but exempts free promotional ones.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Promotion/Recovery/Loyalty certificates expire after 12 months; Purchased certificates never expire.

skill_friction: Step 5 lists 'the requirement contradicts itself' as an ask trigger, but the pre-AskCoworker gate only covers vague requirements; unclear whether to ask before D1/D2 or after. I ran D1/D2 first to give the question evidence (object/picklist options), which cost two calls whose framing (California-address logic) became irrelevant.
The simulated answer did not cover one picklist value (Referral Bonus); the skill has no guidance on partial answers to a question with options, beyond defaulting as an assumption.

R and T answers repeatedly re-raised the same open decisions (DE scheduled-flow capacity, Referral Bonus) and 'prior session' tags on facts I had supplied; the response-handling table says echoed facts are established but does not say how to treat AskCoworker labeling my own supplied facts as '[Verified ... prior session]'.
Timing: R (69s) and T (62s) exceeded the documented ~60 s limit but still returned complete answers; the 'timed out' definition is ambiguous when a call returns after 60 s.

Legal-requirement facts (California Civil Code) are neither platform behavior nor org facts; Rule 3 has no tag for external legal claims, so I used 'assumption (documented platform behavior)' with a qualifier.
